crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Protein Structure Prediction
children.blurb: Protein structure prediction estimates the three-dimensional coordinates of a protein from its amino acid sequence.

children.name: Designing New Molecules
children.blurb: Designing new molecules with AI means using machine learning to propose chemical structures that have a desired biological activity, such as binding to a target protein, while also being synthesizable and safe.

children.name: Simulated Clinical Trials
children.blurb: Simulated clinical trials use computational models of patients, diseases, and treatments to predict how a drug might perform before or instead of a traditional human trial.

children.name: Toxicity Forecasting
children.blurb: Toxicity forecasting covers computational prediction of whether a candidate molecule will cause harm in a living system, including organ damage, mutagenicity, cardiotoxicity, and developmental or reproductive effects.

children.name: Drug Repurposing
children.blurb: Drug repurposing uses AI to find new therapeutic uses for existing approved or investigational drugs.

sections.body: This field applies machine learning to the discovery and assessment of medicines. Artificial intelligence is now predicting how proteins fold, generating candidate molecules, modeling patient populations, forecasting whether a compound might harm cells, and finding new uses for existing drugs. These are not hypothetical demonstrations, they are working systems used in research pipelines. The work spans from the shape of a single protein to the behavior of a drug across a large group of simulated patients. It is a practical set of tools for narrowing the search space before laboratory or human testing.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The most mature area is protein structure prediction, where models can often produce accurate shapes from sequence alone, but they still struggle with complexes, flexible regions, and the effects of mutations. Molecule design can propose novel compounds, yet most candidates fail later in real assays because the models do not capture all biological constraints. Simulated clinical trials are useful for planning and hypothesis testing, but they cannot replace real human trials for safety or efficacy. Toxicity forecasting catches some known failure patterns, but it misses rare or long term effects. Drug repurposing has found plausible matches, though confirming them still requires traditional validation. Across the 803 scientific models tracked on this site, the honest limit is that prediction is not proof.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader wanting to understand how a drug target takes shape would start with Protein Structure Prediction, which explains the models behind folded structures and their confidence scores. Designing New Molecules follows from that, showing how those structures guide the generation of new chemical candidates. Simulated Clinical Trials moves from the molecule to the population, describing how synthetic patient data is used to test ideas before real enrollment. Toxicity Forecasting sits beside that page, covering the models that try to flag dangerous compounds early. Drug Repurposing closes the loop by looking at existing approved drugs and the computational search for new indications. Together these pages trace a path from a protein's shape to a candidate's safety profile and possible second life.
